newsitem.title: FRANCE: French business more bullish but job data ominous.
newsitem.headline: French business more bullish but job data ominous.

text.p: Industrialists gave a considerably more optimistic view of the prospects of rising output in France in a January survey released by the the INSEE statistics office on Thursday, a sign read by economists as promising.

INSEE said its monthly survey showed a marked change of heart from industrialists since December and that they were now more positive about the chances of a general production increase. But it noted they were more cautious about personal prospects.
The good news could pale fast, however, beside figures due on Friday which are expected to show a further rise in French unemployment, already at a record 12.7 percent.

Economists said the INSEE survey was good news and perhaps set the scene for an earlier economic upturn, although some underlined that this was a survey of sentiment rather than an outlook on their investment intentions.
"Business leaders' outlook for production generally has improved markedly compared to the last survey," INSEE said. "Growth in activity should be better supported in the coming months."
"This suggests we're turning into a more positive period for output," said JP Morgan economist David Naude.
The January survey was unlikely to have been influenced by the dollar's recent rise against the franc, which was beneficial for French competitivity and the economy, he said. But others disagreed.

"The recent depreciation of the franc versus the dollar and sterling will have provided the added boost," HSBC Markets said in a note. The swing in business confidence "should help to improve some of the more bearish sentiment", it added.

Philippe Brossard at ABN-Amro said the survey had to be treated with caution but that the signs that stocks were returning to more normal levels supported his above-average forecast of three percent economic growth for 1997.
Brossard said he was expecting job figures on Friday to show a rise of 10,000 or even 20,000 in December and Naude too was predicting a rise of 20,000.
"20,000 could push the (unemployment) rate up to 12.8 percent," Brossard said.
French unemployment rose 20,700 in November to 3.121 million and pushed the unemployement rate to 12.7 from 12.6 percent.
